source_document.body:
Sometimes friends behave badly. When that happens, it is not smart to hurt yourself in retaliation for the friend’s bad behavior. That is true in one’s personal life — and also when it comes to defense strategy.
Consider the case of the Trump administration’s ongoing review of U.S. force posture in Europe and whether Washington will maintain a handful of American naval destroyers forward-stationed in Rota, Spain. Stationing destroyers at Rota helps secure vital American interests in Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East and allows the ships to spend more time conducting missions than traversing back and forth across the Atlantic.
To be clear, the government in Spain has certainly not been working overtime to win favor in Washington. Madrid has stubbornly refused to honor its NATO defense spending commitments, spending a paltry 2% of the country’s gross domestic product on defense. “2.1%, no more, no less,” President Pedro Sanchez said in June . “We fully respect the legitimate desire of other countries to increase their defense investment, but we are not going to do it,” he said.
To make matters worse, earlier this year, Madrid also restricted the U.S. use of Spanish airspace or military bases for operations against Iran.
With the administration openly weighing significant troop reductions across the continent, Spain’s actions may have put it near the top of the candidate list for cuts. But a careful examination makes clear that removing the destroyers based at Rota or closing the base there would be a big mistake.
The base hosts six Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyers, up from four under a 2023 agreement. These vessels, which pack a powerful punch, can conduct anti-air, anti-submarine, and anti-surface warfare missions. The ships’ Aegis Ballistic Missile Defense upgrade enables them to defend against ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and drones. There is no other platform that combines mobile, multi-mission air and missile defense with the endurance to stay on station for months at a time.
Those capabilities have proved pivotal in recent conflicts in the Middle East. Over the past two years, Rota-based destroyers have rotated continuously into the Eastern Mediterranean. As many as four have been on station in those waters, simultaneously defending American interests and supporting the defense of Israel against Iranian ballistic missile attacks. That has saved the lives of Americans and Israelis.
The same ships also provide NATO’s sea-based missile shield against threats from the Middle East. That shield is important to protecting American bases in Europe and their ability to project power into the Middle East and North Africa. The destroyers also serve as the Navy’s forward presence for countering Russian submarine and surface activity in the Mediterranean and increasingly assertive Chinese naval activity off the African coast.
Some might ask whether these vessels can be replaced with European vessels. The answer is no, at least in the short term.
Years of under-resourcing have left European navies a mess. Spain’s own Álvaro de Bazán-class frigates are the most capable European warships, but Europe’s collective sea-based ballistic missile defense capacity remains thin to non-existent, and no European navy can surge Aegis BMD-equivalent coverage into the Eastern Mediterranean the way U.S. destroyers from Rota can.
If Washington brings the American destroyers home to the continental United States, the gap in missile defense coverage for NATO’s southern flank, Israel, and shipping lanes vital to the American economy would not be filled by European navies anytime soon and could potentially create a dangerous security gap for years or even decades.
Plus, a destroyer homeported in Spain, as part of Forward Deployed Naval Force-Europe, spends dramatically more time on station and far less time in transit than a U.S.-based ship that must cross the Atlantic to reach the same waters. That multiplies the combat power each hull generates over its service life.
If anyone in Washington doubts these arguments, consider the current actions of the Pentagon. It has increased the number of destroyers at Rota from four to six, with the final ship arriving only this year. In a recent interview, U.S. 6th Fleet Commander Vice Adm. Jeffrey Anderson suggested the sixth destroyer could not arrive soon enough. Clearly, senior U.S. military leaders believe we need more naval capacity stationed at Rota — not less.
Rota’s submarine support infrastructure, logistics hub, naval special operations support, and air operations also make it one of the most versatile forward installations the U.S. maintains anywhere, facilitating operations across Europe, the High North, Africa, and the Middle East simultaneously from a single location.
None of this means the diplomatic friction with Madrid should be ignored. Washington has every right to press Spain on burden-sharing, defense spending, and foreign policy differences. Washington may need to impose some consequences for Madrid’s decisions, but those should not include self-inflicted wounds that hurt U.S. military readiness and power projection capabilities, making Americans less safe.
The Trump administration should keep six destroyers stationed at Rota. Any other action would be a gift to America’s adversaries.
Rear Adm. (Ret.) Mark Montgomery and Bradley Bowman are senior directors at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies. Montgomery served 32 years in the U.S. Navy, including as deputy director for plans, policy, and strategy (J5) at U.S. European Command. Bowman served in the U.S. Army as a Black Hawk pilot, taught at West Point, and advised members of the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees.

Tesla’s Megapack factory in Brookshire, Texas, is now officially a foreign-trade zone, a US customs program that lets manufacturers defer duties on imported parts. The FTZ Board’s approval, published in the Federal Register on Monday, runs for 14 months.
It’s easy to read this as Tesla getting a pass on tariffs for the Chinese LFP cells inside its Megapacks. Tesla’s own application says otherwise: parts hit by Section 301, 232, or 122 tariffs still pay them.
What Tesla asked for
Tesla filed the request on May 20 for Subzone 84AM, part of FTZ 84 in the Houston area. That’s the factory where Tesla started Megapack 3 production in August , with a planned capacity of 50 GWh per year.
The application lists roughly 80 imported components Tesla wants to bring in under zone procedures, from coolant pumps and transformers to busbars, wiring harnesses, circuit boards and battery cells. Duty rates on those parts go up to 6.5%, while finished Megapacks and Bento inverters range from duty-free to 3.4%.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
That gap is the usual reason companies set up an FTZ. A manufacturer in a zone can normally elect to pay the finished product’s lower rate instead of the rate on each imported part.
The tariff catch
But the application spells out the limit. Components subject to duties under Section 122 of the Trade Act, Section 232 of the Trade Expansion Act, or Section 301 “require subject merchandise to be admitted to FTZs in privileged foreign status,” according to the notice.
Privileged foreign status locks in a part’s own classification and tariff treatment when it enters the zone. So a Chinese LFP cell that ends up in a Megapack sold in the US still pays the Section 301 tariff on Chinese non-EV lithium-ion batteries, which jumped from 7.5% to 25% on January 1, 2026. Tesla just pays it later, when the finished Megapack leaves the zone.
Here’s what Tesla actually gets out of it:
Duties are deferred until a Megapack ships out of the zone, which helps cash flow while the factory ramps up
No US duty on Megapacks exported directly from the zone
The lower finished-product rate on parts that aren’t caught by China, steel, or other special tariffs
No duty on scrap, and fewer customs filings
Useful. Not an exemption.
Same deal everyone else got
The approval came with the same wording the FTZ Board has used all year. Production was “authorized on a limited basis,” and “further subject to a fourteen-month time period.”
Tesla got an identical decision for Megapack and inverter production at Fremont, Livermore and Lathrop in California this summer, with a one-year limit instead. Eastman Chemical, battery pack maker Rose Batteries, and chipmaker Qorvo all received similar time-limited, “limited basis” approvals in 2026.
The 14-month clock puts the expiry around the end of 2027. That’s roughly when LG Energy Solution is due to start supplying Tesla with LFP cells from Michigan under a $4.3 billion contract for Megapack 3, with mass production expected in the second half of 2027.
Tesla’s China cell problem
Tesla hasn’t hidden the issue. When tariffs escalated in April 2025, CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the impact on energy storage would be “outsized since we source lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells from China.” We wrote at the time that Tesla’s only growing business was kneecapped by Trump’s tariffs .
Tesla has since brought up its own LFP cell factory in Nevada , but Taneja said it would only cover a fraction of Tesla’s installed capacity. And Brookshire alone is designed for 50 GWh a year, on top of the 40 GWh Lathrop factory in California.

The U.S. has launched a labor rights investigation into a Mexican packaging manufacturer and announced a separate agreement to address labor rights concerns at an ammunition factory.
The two cases highlight continued enforcement of worker protections under the United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).
The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) announced Monday that it has requested Mexico review allegations that workers at Madobox S.A. de C.V. , a manufacturer of commercial packaging boxes in Uruapan, Michoacán, have been denied their rights to freedom of association and collective bargaining.
As part of the action, USTR directed the U.S. Treasury Department to suspend liquidation of unliquidated customs entries involving goods produced at the Madobox facility.
The suspension is a trade enforcement measure that delays final customs processing and duty assessments on affected imports. It does not necessarily prevent the goods from entering the U.S.
The investigation was initiated under the USMCA’s Rapid Response Labor Mechanism , which allows the United States to challenge alleged violations of workers’ rights at specific facilities in Mexico.
Union alleges interference, retaliatory firings
The U.S. investigation follows a Sept. 30 petition filed by a Mexican labor union affiliated with the Confederación Central Nacional (COCENA).
The union alleges that Madobox interfered with workers’ organizing activities by arranging a collective bargaining agreement without worker participation, coercing and misleading employees about their labor rights, and unlawfully dismissing workers in retaliation for union activity.
After reviewing the petition, the U.S. Interagency Labor Committee for Monitoring and Enforcement determined there was sufficient credible evidence to invoke the USMCA enforcement process.
Mexico has 10 days from the Nov. 2 request to agree to conduct a review. If it accepts, the Mexican government has 45 days from Nov. 2 to complete its investigation.
Madobox manufactures corrugated cardboard packaging for agricultural products, including avocados, mangoes, berries and tomatoes, according to its website. Based in Uruapan, a major avocado-producing region, the company supplies packaging used in agricultural supply chains, including products destined for export markets.
US, Mexico reach agreement in separate factory dispute
In a separate announcement Monday, USTR said the U.S. and Mexico reached a memorandum of understanding addressing labor rights concerns at Industrias Tecnos S.A. de C.V. , an ammunition manufacturer in Cuernavaca, Morelos.
The agreement follows a labor dispute dating to May 2024, when a Mexican union filed a petition alleging workers at the facility were being denied collective bargaining and freedom of association rights.
The U.S. requested Mexico review the allegations in June 2024. Mexican authorities subsequently found no denial of rights, prompting Washington to request a dispute settlement panel under the USMCA.
The new agreement establishes corrective measures intended to protect workers and prevent future violations.
Under the agreement, Industrias Tecnos must verify that dismissed workers receive compensation owed under Mexican law, implement workplace neutrality policies, train employees on labor rights and establish confidential complaint mechanisms.
Mexico also agreed to monitor compliance, review determinations involving dismissed workers and conduct additional training for supervisors, human resources personnel and other company officials.
The memorandum established an Oct. 15 deadline for completing the corrective actions, although USTR’s Nov. 2 announcement did not specify whether all measures had been implemented.
Industrias Tecnos manufactures Aguila Ammunition, which serves sporting, hunting, law enforcement and military markets. Texas Armament & Technology, a U.S.-based distributor, identifies itself as Aguila’s exclusive master distributor in North America and other markets.
Why it matters: USMCA labor enforcement can create customs compliance risks for Mexican manufacturers and their U.S. customers, adding another consideration for cross-border supply chains.

By: David Cassels November 3, 2026
Nouveau Monde Graphite (TSX: NOU; NYSE: NMG) has obtained a Quebec mining lease granting extraction rights at its Matawinie graphite project, where construction is underway ahead of a planned production ramp-up by the end of 2028.
The project, around 120 km north of Montreal near Saint-Michel-des-Saints, is designed to produce about 106,000 tonnes of graphite concentrate annually over 25 years. Construction began in April, followed by a final investment decision in May, the company said.
“This milestone is the result of several years of dialogue and close collaboration with the Atikamekw community of Manawan, the municipality of Saint-Michel-des-Saints, and Quebec’s regulatory authorities,” founder, president and CEO Eric Desaulniers said in Monday’s lease announcement .
Matawinie is intended to supply a domestic graphite industry serving battery manufacturers and other customers. The company also plans a Bécancour plant capable of producing 13,000 tonnes of battery materials annually, although a final investment decision on that project remains pending. Matawinie would become Canada’s largest operating natural graphite mine, according to Nouveau Monde.
Shares closed 2.3% weaker at $1.27 in Toronto on Monday, reversing an earlier gain. They were at $1.26 Tuesday morning, valuing the company at nearly $415 million (US$297 million).
Construction advances
Preliminary construction began on April 13, with work progressing within budget as of the company’s second-quarter update. Construction and commissioning are expected to take about 31 months, leading to the start of the production ramp-up by the end of 2028, the company said in its August filing .
Quebec authorized Matawinie by decree in 2021, following a public review conducted in 2020 by the Bureau d’audiences publiques sur l’environnement. The mining lease was issued by the province’s Ministry of Natural Resources and Forests.
The company signed an impact and benefit agreement with the Atikamekw community of Manawan in December 2024. It provides for community participation in environmental monitoring, alongside employment, training and business opportunities, according to Nouveau Monde.
Environmental scrutiny
The project’s design includes water reuse, progressive restoration, biodiversity protection and co-disposal of tailings and waste rock, the company says.

2027 Suzuki GSX-10R Is All About the Brutal Engine Power of a True Sportsbike
25 photos
Photo: Suzuki
The GSX-R family of Suzuki sportsbikes will have a new member come the summer of next year. Shown for the first time in the metal at the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show that takes place this week in Milan, Italy, the newcomer seems, at least on paper, as unforgiving to the competition as it is brutal in terms of specs.
Drawing on the GSX-R1000R , the new two-wheeler is built around a new aluminum frame that comes complete with a new swingarm and a new subframe. Inside it there is a fresh interpretation of the K5 engine, the inline four-cylinder that in this application is rated at 150 horsepower at 11,000 rpm and 106 Nm of torque at 9,250 rpm.
The engine has been revised inside and out, as, according to the Japanese bike maker, it not only needs to fulfill the demands of today's riders, be them for the tracks or public roads, but it also needs to be future-proof against the introduction of upcoming alcohol-based fuels.
To that end, the heart of the machine comes with new cams, camshafts, cam chain sprocket, cylinder head, barrels, and cases. The new setup ties into a four-into-one exhaust and a transmission controlled through Suzuki's Slipper Clutch Assist system.
The new motorcycle has been propped on cast aluminum wheels sized 17 inches on both ends, shod in Bridgestone Battlax Hypersport S23 tires. Brembo braking hardware is connected to both of them, with the front one also tied to fully adjustable 43 mm KYB forks and the one at the opposite end to a shock specifically designed for it.
The bike's operation is governed by an electronics package that bundles together a six-axis IMU with slide, roll torque, traction, and wheelie control, among others. When it comes to riding position, the new bike copies a lot from the GSX-R1000R, including when it comes to seat (located 810 mm off the ground, 15 mm lower than on the base bike), handlebar, and footpeg triangle.
When it comes to the way it looks, the new sportsbike is heavily inspired by its sibling, but also throws in some specific design cues. There are LED lights all around, front air intakes to help it breathe and cool, a fresh cowl design, and a rounded profile for the entire front section.
Suzuki says it will make the new bike available to riders in the summer of next year, so there's plenty of waiting to do until the two-wheeler actually gets here. When it lands, it will be offered in three color schemes: Pearl Vigor Blue and Metallic Mystic Silver, Pearl Pulse Red and Solid Iron Grey, and Glass Sparkle Black and Metallic Galaxy Grey.
Seeing how the official launch of the model is more than half a year away, Suzuki makes no mention of how much it will charge for the GSX-10R. For the record, the GSX-R1000R presently goes for around $18,000.

Are you still thinking about sprucing up your life with a cool, modern-classic muscle car, but find the latest S650 Ford Mustang and its predecessor, the S550, a bit too bland, and not that cool? Well, in that case, how about an S197?
This is the code for the fifth-generation model, which was assembled between 2004 and 2014. Production took place at the Flat Rock factory in Michigan, USA. The company offered it in two body styles, a two-door coupe and a two-door convertible, and the S197 II was offered with a pair of V6 engines, as well as several V8s. The engine family included the 5-liter Coyote, as well as a pair of supercharged units, and depending on the spec, they were offered with manual and automatic transmissions.
Pictured above is a 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 , a model that came with the usual Coyote V8, albeit in an enhanced version, featuring plenty of modifications. The output was rated at 444 horsepower (450 ps/331 kW), and the thrust was 380 pound-feet (515 Nm). Various tests from back in the day revealed that the 0-60 mph (0-97 kph) took a little over 4 seconds, and the quarter mile was dealt with in just over 12 seconds. The top speed was capped at (155 mph (250 kph), but the model could easily exceed it.
A six-speed manual transmission channels everything to the rear wheels, and besides the extra oomph, this model also featured a modified chassis setup, sat a bit closer to the asphalt, rode on 19-inch alloys, and came with a special aero package inspired by the Boss302R racer. Some of the goodies included the Bluetooth connectivity, a premium audio system, power-adjustable seats at the front, SiriusXM, and others. The Sync system was added on later models.
Photo: Cars&Bids According to the listing, the Ford Mustang Boss 302 in question comes with the factory wheels, has a 3.73:1 limited-slip rear axle, a manually adjustable suspension, Brembo brakes at the front, stripes on the hood and profile, air conditioning, cruise control, and an Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel. It has a Race Red exterior, a Charcoal Black cabin, a clean Texas title, and is located in Willis, TX.
And it has been living in Texas its entire life, because it has a single owner in the papers, and this definitely adds up to the hype. The vendor represents the first and only owner, and it is unknown why they want their muscle car gone, though they have probably gotten bored with it. This machine was $42,995 new, according to the attached window sticker, and this model is now worth from over $30,000 to roughly $50,000, depending on the usual factors that influence a car’s value.
It is worth noting that the tires on this 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 carry 2011 date codes on them, and this is something that the next owner will have to take care of, especially if they want to enjoy the vehicle in the open. The odometer read only 520 miles (~840 km) at the time of cataloging, but it is inaccurate. The vendor blames it on a clerical error, and says that they have filed a dispute claim with Carfax.
Photo: Cars&Bids Besides the muscle car, the next owner will also get the OEM car cover, one key, one red key, and the owner’s manual. And you know what to do if you want it, don’t you? Actually, you don’t, not yet, anyway, because we haven’t revealed this aspect yet. This ride was advertised on Cars&Bids as part of an auction that ended on November 2, 2026. When the gavel hit the table, the highest bid was $37,250. And since the reserve was not met, the muscle car failed to change hands.
As a result, we can assume that the seller likely wants more than $40,000, and it is up to you to decide whether it is worth that kind of money or not. Nevertheless, the chances of encountering a 2013 model year Ford Mustang Boss 302 with a single owner in the papers since new are close to zero, and if this matters, then you may want to make an offer. After all, what is the worse than they can do? Decline it?
The red-on-black vehicle with its clean Texas title and one owner in the papers, as well as the mileage discrepancy mentioned above, is still for grabs, and if you really want it, then you should get in touch with the vendor by accessing this link , which will redirect you to the quoted website. But before clicking that link, let us know how much this 2013 Ford Mustang Boss 302 is really worth in your opinion by dropping a line (or more) in the comments section at the bottom of the page. Keep in mind that it failed to sell for $37,250.

Touquoy gold mine site in Moose River, Nova Scotia. ( Image courtesy of St Barbara. )
By: Staff Writer November 3, 2026
St Barbara (ASX: SBM) is scheduled to resume processing stockpiled ore at its Touquoy gold mine in Nova Scotia on Tuesday, as a federal assessment requirement raises questions over the timetable for its proposed 15-Mile processing hub.
The restart covers about three million tonnes of previously mined ore and does not authorize new extraction. Mill refurbishment and tailings-line construction are complete, with commissioning and operations expected to ramp up through November and December, the company said Monday.
The federal decision was “very disappointing for both St Barbara and the Province of Nova Scotia,” managing director and CEO Andrew Strelein said, arguing that it conflicts with Ottawa’s commitment to avoid duplicate reviews.
The stockpiles offer a near-term return to gold production while St Barbara advances a larger regional development. The proposed hub would process ore from 15-Mile and two satellite projects, Old Austen and Old Mitchell, formerly known as Beaver Dam and Cochrane Hill.
St Barbara shares closed 2.8% stronger at A$0.73 in Sydney on Tuesday, following a 14% decline on Monday.
Stockpile restart
Nova Scotia granted industrial approval in April to subsidiary Atlantic Mining Nova Scotia to process the ore left at Touquoy when operations stopped in 2023. The approval restricts activity to the existing disturbed footprint, with processing waste to be deposited in the open pit.
Reclamation began in 2024 and will continue outside the mill area during processing. The province holds a $79.9-million reclamation bond, following an earlier cleanup bond dispute with the company.
As a contingency against delays at 15-Mile, St Barbara is preparing to seek provincial permission to resume mining within Touquoy’s existing open-pit footprint. Additional ore could supplement the stockpiles and extend production beyond 2027, the company said.
Federal assessment
The 15-Mile proposal entered the federal planning process in June. On Oct. 30, the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada determined that a federal impact assessment is required.
Potential effects on fish and fish habitat, migratory birds and Indigenous peoples’ traditional land use warrant further assessment, the agency said in its decision notice . The project could also affect Indigenous rights, heritage, health and social or economic conditions.
The agency said it would work with Nova Scotia to reduce duplication while meeting legislative and consultation obligations, taking into account the federal-provincial assessment agreement.
Federal officials have indicated the assessment can finish before the targeted mid-2028 construction start, according to St Barbara. The company plans to meet both governments over the next three weeks to assess the implications for costs and timing.
St Barbara supports Bill C-39 , which proposes a maximum one-year period for federal reviews and decisions once comprehensive applications, studies and required information have been submitted. The proposed deadline would not begin with a project’s initial filing, according to the federal government.
Underground potential
St Barbara also announced an initial underground resource at Old Austen on Monday, identifying mineralization outside its previously reported open-pit resource.
The November estimate contains 2 million indicated tonnes grading 3 grams gold per tonne for 190,000 oz., and 2.8 million inferred tonnes at 3.7 grams for 330,000 oz., according to the company’s resource update .
The combined 520,000 oz. adds a potential underground source of ore to the regional development plans, although the estimate is a resource rather than a mining reserve.
Drilling planned for spring and summer 2027 will aim to upgrade the inferred material and test deeper extensions towards the Mud Lake fault, the company said.

All the key numbers at Expeditors International pointed upward in the third quarter at the logistics and freight forwarding company.
Revenue year-on-year was up 42%, to $4.1 billion at the asset-light customs broker and freight forwarder.
Despite the fact that the cost of transportation rose 49%, a faster rate than revenues, and salaries climbed 15%, operating income rose 55% to $445.4 million, up from $288 million a year ago.
Diluted earnings per share were up 61% to $2.65 per share.
According to SeekingAlpha, that EPS figure beat consensus estimates by 42 cts/share, while the revenue of $4.11 billion was higher than consensus estimates by $510 million.
Stock doesn’t move higher
Despite topping those forecasts, Expeditors’ (NYSE: EXPD) stock in early trading showed little positive reaction. At approximately 9:50 a.m. EST, it was down 0.76%, or $1.52, to $199.04. The stock is trading at about a 28.9 P/E ratio for the trailing twelve months, which is considered slightly higher than the market as a whole.
But the company’s stock had a strong run for several months. Coming into Tuesday’s trading, Expeditors was up about 3.9% in the last month, 17.2% in the last three months and 63.3% in the last year, according to data from Barchart.
Volume picked up significantly for Expeditors as the quarter wore on. The year-over-year increase for airfreight was 8% in July, 13% in August and 19% in September, for an overall increase of 13%.
The growth rates in ocean freight were smaller but still ended up higher than they started. The July and August increase was 5%, with an increase in September of 12%. The overall increase in ocean freight was 12%.
More workers
Employee headcount rose slightly year-on-year. The total was 20,463, up from 20,170 a year ago, an increase of 1.4%. But there were declines in Global Technology–down to 1,151 from 1,483–and corporate, which dropped to 396 workers from 419.
Expeditors does not conduct an earnings call with analysts.
In the prepared statement released with the earnings, CEO Daniel Wall said Expeditors’ market share has been rising, “particularly in markets where we have made a strategic focus.”
Expeditors’ strong performance in the past 1.5 years has been attributed in part to its knowledge of tariffs and how they work, a strength that has been particularly valuable in times where such levies have been implemented and taken off in rapid succession.
“While we have thrived during periods of significant disruption throughout our history, the strength of demand for our products and services is what really drove Q3 performance,” Wall said.
AI tailwinds
He also cited the AI boom as a reason for the strong performance. .
“Demand from certain customers, such as the hyperscalers, has been outpacing the market overall, but we have been very deliberate to expand our customer base across our global network and further diversify our revenues.
On the specific growth areas, Wall said airfreight demand was helped by “record global air tonnage,” citing South Asia as a key market. Wall cited “hyperscaler demand.” “Air capacity remains constrained by limited fleet expansion and ongoing new aircraft delivery delays,” he added.
Wall also said U.S.-China e-commerce trade, which was impacted by the elimination of the U.S. break on de minimis imports , is back to the levels it was before the May 2025 shift in policy.”
“Adding geopolitical events to this mix, airfreight rates remained elevated during the quarter, with demand outpacing available capacity,” Wall said.
The ocean freight part of Expeditors’ business was impacted by three Asian typhoons, Wall said. But “the strength of our global network and world class operating teams enabled us to maintain service continuity and respond effectively as conditions deteriorated,” he added.

The Swiss contract development and manufacturing organization will more than double its U.S. footprint by acquiring the Merck KGaA plants.
Lonza has struck a deal to buy five U.S. manufacturing plants from Merck KGaA at a valuation ranging in the low- to mid-triple-digit millions in Swiss francs.
Responding to an analyst on a conference call Tuesday, Lonza CEO Wolfgang Wienand said somewhere in the middle of the CHF 100 million ($122 million) to CHF 600 million ($732 million) range “would be roundabout the right view on the acquisition price.” In return, Lonza will acquire U.S. production sites specializing in bioconjugation, payload-linkers and viral vectors.
“We view this as another highly attractive strategic acquisition for Lonza that meaningfully strengthens its competitive positioning across several attractive, high-growth modalities, positioning it well for its next leg of growth,” William Blair analysts said in a Tuesday morning note to investors.
Buying Merck KGaA’s bioconjugate plant in St. Louis, Missouri, and high-potency payload-linker facilities in Madison and Verona, Wisconsin, will strengthen Lonza’s antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) production capabilities. Currently, Lonza’s ADC capabilities center on its site in Visp, Switzerland. Lonza is also buying Merck KGaA’s viral vector plant in Carlsbad, California, and aseptic fill-finish site in Indianapolis, Indiana.
About 1,100 employees will transfer to Lonza as part of the deal. Lonza, which will employ more than 6,000 people across nine U.S. sites once the deal closes, expects the acquired facilities to contribute about CHF 250 million ($305 million) in sales in 2028.

While the facilities will initially be less profitable than Lonza is today, the contract manufacturer expects to bring margins in line with the rest of its business by the time the Merck KGaA sites reach peak sales in the mid-2030s. Lonza’s belief that it can grow sales at the plants rests on its assessment of capacity use and forecasts for market growth.
Capacity utilization is “way below the level we believe can be achieved,” Wienand said. By integrating the sites into the Lonza network, the CEO expects to “broaden the customer pipeline, increase utilization and progressively increase sales and profitability.”
Lonza expects the global bioconjugation market to grow from around $30 billion today to around $110 billion by 2033, Wienand said. Establishing end-to-end drug substance manufacturing for ADCs in the U.S. will enable Lonza to engage customers earlier, work on more programs and provide clinical and commercial-scale production options on both sides of the Atlantic, the CEO added.
When Lonza acquired a U.S. plant from Roche in 2024, it agreed to supply the drugs that the pharma company produced at the site. The Merck KGaA deal is different. Christian Seufert, head of advanced synthesis at Lonza, advised an analyst against assuming that there is a contract in place with Merck KGaA, noting that “the business was primarily focused on third-party sales and third-party revenue.”
There was an almost three-year gap between the Roche and Merck KGaA deals, but Wienand said Lonza “will not hesitate” to act if it finds an attractive takeover target while integrating the five U.S. sites. The company has the bandwidth to work on deals in parallel to the Merck KGaA agreement, which it expects to close in mid-2027.

Pouring a gold bar. Canada was among several countries recording substantial gains in output. Credit: iStock
Posted By: Colin McClelland November 3, 2026
Canadian gold production jumped 22% in the third quarter as new mines increased output, outpacing global growth even as rising costs made ounces more expensive to produce.
Recently commissioned operations including Equinox Gold’s (TSX, NYSE-A: EQX) Valentine mine in Newfoundland and Labrador and B2Gold’s (TSX: BTO; NYSE-A: BTG) Goose mine in Nunavut helped drive the increase, alongside stronger production from existing mines, the World Gold Council said Tuesday. Worldwide mine output rose 3% to a third-quarter record of 1,071 tonnes.
“Mine production could reach another record high, but the overall supply response should remain modest, with recycling still subdued,” the council said in its latest quarterly assessment .
Canada’s growth shows how new operations are adding meaningful volumes while some established mining countries struggle with lower grades and changing mine plans. Yet increased mine production has not translated into more total supply: weaker recycling and a further reduction in producers’ outstanding hedges pushed the global total 1% lower to 1,369 tonnes.
Canadian growth
Valentine entered commercial production in November last year, giving this year’s third quarter a much larger contribution than the commissioning period a year earlier. The Newfoundland operation is expected to produce 140,000 to 150,000 oz. this year, according to Equinox’s operating outlook .
Canada was among several countries recording substantial gains. Indonesian output increased 21%, helped by higher grades and production at Batu Hijau, the start of Pani Gold and recovering output at Grasberg. Chilean production rose 19%, supported by Salares Norte and the newly commissioned Fenix operation, the council said.
Those increases contrasted with a 12% decline in Australia and a 7% fall in the United States. Lower-grade mining and production sequencing weighed on both countries, including at Cadia in Australia and Nevada Gold Mines and Round Mountain in the U.S.
Global mine production was 2% higher over the first nine months, putting the industry on course for a full-year record unless widespread disappointments emerge in the fourth quarter, the council said.
Costs climb
The additional output comes at a higher cost. Average industry all-in sustaining costs reached a record $1,930 (C$2,698) per oz. in the second quarter, up 22% from a year earlier, according to Metals Focus data cited by the council. The figures, which lag production data by a quarter, showed the fastest annual cost increase since early 2013.
Higher energy and consumable prices, along with increased sustaining capital spending, contributed to the rise.
BMO Capital Markets’ latest GoldPages estimates point in the same direction. Production-weighted sustaining costs for producers covered by the bank are forecast to average $1,795 per oz. this year, 16% more than in 2025. Including development capital, average all-in costs are forecast to rise 22% to $2,298 per ounce.
The BMO figures cover a different group of companies and a full year, so they are not directly comparable with the council’s quarterly industry estimate. The bank forecasts some relief next year, with sustaining costs easing to $1,764 per ounce.
Gold prices remain well above those cost measures. Bullion averaged $4,262 per oz. in the third quarter, 23% more than a year earlier, according to the council. However, sustaining costs exclude development spending and do not measure a company’s full cash requirements.
Recycling retreats
Recycled supply fell 8% to about 314 tonnes in the third quarter, its lowest level since late 2023. The decline outweighed the increase in mined gold, alongside an estimated 17-tonne reduction in outstanding producer hedges.
Recycling remained subdued despite historically high prices. In India, some owners preferred to pledge gold as collateral, while jewellery exchanges allowed buyers to fund new purchases with old pieces. Expectations of higher prices also discouraged selling, the council said.
Chinese recycling fell 20% from a year earlier. Trading in old jewellery to offset a new tax on jewellery sales also encouraged exchanges rather than outright sales.
Producers’ aggregate hedge book declined for an eleventh consecutive quarter. Deliveries into maturing contracts and restructuring of existing positions contributed to the reduction, while miners showed limited appetite to lock in future prices.
Central banks buy
On the demand side, central banks provided the strongest offset to weaker consumer buying. Their estimated purchases rose 42% to 321 tonnes, lifting nine-month buying to 675 tonnes, 6% above the same period last year.
China and Poland together added about 104 tonnes to disclosed holdings. China’s purchases extended the accelerating accumulation evident in its September figures.
However, reported purchases accounted for only about 120 tonnes of the quarterly total. The remaining 63% reflected estimated unreported activity, limiting the visibility into which countries were buying.
Gold-backed exchange-traded funds added 211 tonnes after second-quarter outflows, although that was 6% less than a year earlier. The inflows extended the investment divergence seen in September, when fund buying persisted despite falling bullion prices.
Bar-and-coin demand fell 19% to 268 tonnes, while jewellery consumption dropped 17% to 313 tonnes, the weakest third quarter in the council’s series. Total demand, including over-the-counter activity, fell 1%.
The council halved its forecast for this year’s increase in investment demand to 200 tonnes from 400 tonnes as bar-and-coin buying slowed. It raised its expectation for central bank purchases, which it now expects to at least match last year.
That buying could help support prices, but the council cautioned against treating it as a guarantee.
“Purchases nevertheless appear sensitive to price,” the council said. “This pattern could provide some price support and stability, although the relationship is not sufficiently stable to imply a firm floor for the gold price.”

A new survey of 103 industry experts has found that artificial intelligence is moving beyond trials in container ports and terminals, but measurable financial returns remain scarce.
While 44% of respondents said their organizations had reached the scaling stage or beyond, Boston Consulting Group reported , only 4% reported measurable earnings gains and just 11% systematically tracked AI’s contribution to efficiency or margins.
The findings highlight a measurement gap as operators expand their use of technology to process shipping documents, anticipate equipment failures and support operational decisions. Conducted in August 2026 with the Terminal Industry Committee 4.0 (TIC4.0), an international, non-profit association established in 2019 and based in Brussels, the survey covered experts across five continents, including terminal operators, port authorities, container shipping lines and port vendors. BCG published the findings in October.
The study assessed 43 AI use cases. Extracting data from shipping documents was being explored or implemented by 62% of respondents, while 48% were exploring or using AI to predict failures in equipment such as cranes and straddle carriers.
Respondents reported benefits primarily in day-to-day operations: 74% identified improved operational efficiency, 44% faster decision-making and 41% cost reductions. Just 18% reported an improvement in customer experience, suggesting that adoption has so far focused more on internal performance than customer-facing services.
Those reported improvements have not generally translated into documented earnings gains. An operator may identify faster workflows or reduced downtime without systematically establishing how much those improvements contribute to financial performance.
Unclear returns remain the biggest obstacle
Uncertainty over return on investment was the most frequently cited barrier to wider adoption, named by 41% of respondents. Data quality followed at 32%, while 30% cited difficulties integrating AI with existing systems.
The survey also revealed a divide between senior executives and colleagues closer to implementation. Among respondents below C-suite level, 44% identified unclear returns as a barrier, compared with 21% of senior leaders. The findings suggest that confidence at the top is not always matched by a clear business case for the teams responsible for deploying the technology.
Investment plans nevertheless indicate continued interest. Some 59% of respondents planned to hire or train AI specialists, 55% were allocating funding to research and development, and 47% planned to add AI modules to existing systems.
Moving from pilots to operational value
BCG and TIC4.0 recommended that operators establish evidence of value before expanding deployments, using performance baselines accepted by the operational managers closest to the work. They also called for investment in shared data foundations across businesses, rather than disconnected projects at individual terminals.
The report identified daily operational workflows as an important area for future development. The share of respondents identifying AI integration into those workflows as beneficial was expected to rise from 60% today to 74%, while interest in forecasting operational conditions and their causes was expected to increase from 49% to 67%.
Customer demand could provide another route to value. Freight forwarders were cited by 61% of respondents as a source of demand for AI-enabled terminal services, followed by third-party logistics providers at 58% and container shipping lines at 52%. BCG urged operators to develop services alongside customers, linking technical capabilities to needs for which there is already commercial interest.
Why it matters: For ports, expanding AI deployment is only part of the task; operators also need reliable evidence that it improves the business.

Drill core from the Ramp Zone at Collective Mining's Guayabales project, about 198 km northwest of Bogotá. Credit: Collective Mining
Posted By: Henry Lazenby November 3, 2026
Collective Mining (TSX, Nasdaq: CNL) shares jumped 13% Tuesday after the company reported a 154.3-metre gold intercept at Colombia’s Apollo project, its broadest high-grade interval yet in the deep Ramp Zone.
Hole APC174-D4 returned 12.44 grams gold per tonne and 11 grams silver over the interval, starting about 1,208 metres below surface, the company reported Tuesday. Apollo is part of the company’s Guayabales project, about 198 km northwest of Bogotá.
“This hole did not run out of gold; it ran out of rods,” Executive Chairman Ari Sussman said in a news release. “We believe the Ramp Zone is only beginning to show us its true potential.”
National Bank of Canada Capital Markets analyst Don DeMarco said the hole delivered Apollo’s strongest combination of grade and drilled length to date. The results were “hinting that the Ramp Zone could be bigger and higher grade than the maiden resource,” he wrote Tuesday.
Drill limits
Collective shares rose to $15.71 (US$11.50) by mid-Tuesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about $1.5 billion. DeMarco maintained his outperform rating and $32 share-price target, citing the potential for a major mining district while cautioning that economic and feasibility studies are still ahead.
The drilling is testing whether Apollo’s deeper gold-rich zones could support underground mining alongside shallower material outlined for an open pit. Higher grades could strengthen that case, but Collective still needs an economic assessment to establish what it would cost to build and operate the project.
The main interval included 30.45 metres at 38.47 grams gold from about 1,339 metres below surface. That section returned substantially higher grades than predicted by the resource model, Collective said. The comparison applies only to the blocks crossed by the hole and doesn’t revise the resource estimate.
The hole finished in lower-grade mineralization outside the resource, returning a final 12.2 metres at 0.71 gram gold before reaching the rig’s drilling limit. Reported intervals are downhole lengths, with estimated true widths ranging from 60% to 100%.
Initial resource
Apollo’s initial estimate , effective Aug. 31, outlines 37 million indicated tonnes grading 1.38 grams gold and 24.4 grams silver per tonne, plus 0.14% copper and 0.011% tungsten trioxide. That contains 1.64 million oz. gold and 29 million oz. silver.
A further 48.2 million inferred tonnes grade 1.6 grams gold and 8.39 grams silver, with 0.03% copper and 0.002% tungsten trioxide, containing 2.47 million oz. gold and 13 million oz. silver.
The estimate separates material considered suitable for an open pit from two underground components, including the Ramp Zone.
Underground access
Collective expects to begin construction of the roughly 3-km exploration tunnel this month. The planned route would provide drilling platforms for the Trap and Plutus targets before reaching Apollo’s Ramp Zone, allowing the company to test mineralization from underground.
The company plans to release an updated resource between late next year and early 2028, incorporating about 100,000 metres of additional drilling, followed by a preliminary economic assessment. It has said this year’s planned 90,000-metre drill program is fully funded.
Collective is targeting an environmental licence application in the second half of next year.

BYD's $3 Million Hypercar Crashes at 224 MPH, Driver Walks Away
24 photos
Photo: CarNewsChina | YouTube
A BYD Yangwang U9 Xtreme, valued at roughly $3 million, violently crashed during a high-speed testing session in China. The test was supposed to precede an intended open-road record attempt, targeting the 310 mph (500 kph) barrier. The automaker will most likely cancel the attempt that was set to take place in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.
Crowned the fastest EV at Nurburgring last year, The vehicle was undergoing preliminary high-speed testing at an undisclosed track in China that BYD was using to push the car into the 261 - 280 mph (420 - 450 kph) phase before shipping it to the UAE for the official 311 mph (500 kph) attempt.
BYD's test driver Jiang Wen, a 23-year veteran driver for the company, was behind the wheel. He survived the crash without serious injuries and was seen walking away from the wreckage. He later received a routine hospital checkup.
The driver explained that the vehicle lost traction at extreme speed. When he lifted off the accelerator to correct it, he lost the rear end, which began to swerve out of control, hitting the left-side guardrail at around 224 mph (360 kph). It then spun out and slammed into the right-side guardrail.
Photo: CarNewsChina | YouTube The $3 million electric hypercar was entirely destroyed as the rear axle detached from the rest of the vehicle. The front end, along with the entire body, is now a pile of metal. However, the carbon fier/silicon carbide-based passenger safety cell held up and prevented cabin intrusion, keeping the driver safe. The battery pack was not punctured, and no fire followed the crash.
The U9 Xtreme previously hit an unofficial/certified top speed of 308.4 mph (496.22 kph) at the Automotive Testing Papenburg facility in Germany back in September 2025. The BYD engineers fine-tuned the powertrain and were ready to take it to the next level in the UAE.
Breaking speed records were what the U9 Xtreme was actually built for. The car features a highly advanced, ultra-high-voltage powertrain built for record-breaking speed. Sitting on a 1,200-volt silicon carbide platform, the hypercar is set in motion by a quad-motor setup, with each motor independently powering a wheel.
The system produces a massive 2,977 horsepower (3,018 metric horsepower) and 2,212 pound-feet (3,000 Newton meters) of torque. That makes it rocket from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 kph) in under 2.0 seconds and max out at 308.4 mph (496.22 kph) in standard configuration.

Designed for the global market, GA-ASI’s Gambit 6 UCAV is built to fly with crewed and uncrewed aircraft to secure the modern battlespace with precision air-to-ground strike capability. (Artist’s rendering)
The threats faced by crewed fighters on today’s battlefield have proliferated at a staggering pace. That’s why the time has come for the U.S., along with its allies in Europe and across the globe, to adopt autonomous Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS) at scale.
The modern air defense environment has grown dramatically more lethal. Powerful radars, highly capable anti-air missiles, and loitering munitions now menace even the most advanced tactical aircraft. Ground-based, long-range missiles can threaten fixed targets, such as airfields, across entire regions.
These capabilities are no longer limited to major powers with advanced technology — they have trickled down to second-tier nations and even terrorist groups.
The reemergence of industrial-scale warfare demands an industrial-scale response. Yet the cost of still-vital crewed fighters has become unaffordable even to nations with world-leading defense budgets such as the United States.
Crewed-uncrewed teaming offers a solution. By using uncrewed fighters designed for simplicity and mass production, nations can affordably overwhelm, disperse, and eliminate enemy air defenses while diverting enemy tactical aircraft away from crewed fighters and bombers.
GA-ASI’s Gambit Series of Uncrewed Aerial Combat Vehicles (UCAVs) was developed to address precisely this challenge. Each Gambit is a mission-focused uncrewed combat aircraft designed to operate alongside crewed fighters.
A Modular Approach to Affordable Mass
Rather than building a single aircraft for every mission, GA-ASI created a modular family of uncrewed jet fighters with variants optimized for distinct operational roles.
This approach avoids the costs of multi-mission aircraft, which in many cases are not best suited for roles that require flying into the teeth of enemy air defenses. It also retains common hardware across the family. Indeed, Gambit strikes the right balance between cost and capability.
About 70 percent of Gambit’s key components, including the landing gear, baseline avionics, and core airframe structures, are shared among its variants. This commonality simplifies production, lowers lifecycle costs, and accelerates the creation of mission-specific aircraft.
The family includes:
Gambit 1 : Long-endurance ISR
Gambit 2 : Air-to-air combat
Gambit 3 : Adversary air training
Gambit 4 : Stealth combat reconnaissance
Gambit 5 : Carrier-based operations
Gambit 6 : Air-to-ground missions
Gambit 6 was developed specifically to meet the needs of European nations facing advanced, industrial-scale threats on their eastern front. It has been optimized for electronic warfare, suppression of enemy air defenses, and deep precision strike in contested environments.
Each Gambit features a signature-reducing internal weapons bay that supports the integration of electronic warfare systems, precision-guided munitions, sensors, and autonomy software.
The modular architecture and signature-reducing weapons bay allow for easy integration of advanced autonomy, sensors, and weapons systems, ensuring the aircraft can adapt to a wide range of operational scenarios.
Operational Experience and Production Readiness
The U.S. Air Force recently awarded an initial production contract to GA-ASI for its FQ-42 Vengeance Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA), a derivative of Gambit 2. This means that GA-ASI is already in serial production of the world’s first uncrewed fighter jet.
The FQ-42 Vengeance CCA is now in full-scale production for the U.S. Air Force.
GA-ASI’s position in the CCA market is rooted in nearly two decades of development, both through independent research and development and in collaboration with the U.S. Air Force.
Leveraging its more than five million square feet of fully operational manufacturing facilities, GA-ASI is ready to begin producing aircraft at scale the moment a contract is awarded.
Optimized for European Requirements
For European customers, Gambit is a platform that supports sovereign integration and industrial participation.
General Atomics’ German affiliate, General Atomics AeroTec Systems GmbH, could support local assembly, integration, and testing for German programs, while partnerships with European industry would enable integration of national sensors, mission systems, and autonomy software.
GA-ASI’s CCA solution for Europe leverages the U.S. Air Force’s FQ-42 and would be assembled in Germany in partnership with European industry.
GA-ASI expects Gambit 6 airframes to be available for international procurement beginning in 2027, with European missionized versions deliverable by 2029.
By choosing Gambit, European nations gain a combat-ready, sovereign platform that combines cutting-edge technology with domestic industrial growth and strategic autonomy.
With its unmatched capabilities, production readiness, and commitment to indigenous integration, Gambit represents a scalable solution designed to counter today’s threats and address tomorrow’s challenges.

Partial view of the Eagle River mine site. Credit: Wesdome Gold Mines.
Posted By: FREDERIC TOMESCO November 3, 2026
Wesdome Gold Mines (TSX: WDO; US-OTC: WDOFF) has extended gold mineralization near existing workings at its Eagle River mine in Ontario, opening potential mining areas that could require less development to reach.
Hole 26-925-10 in the western extension of the 800 zone cut 10.6 metres grading 8.25 grams gold per tonne from 298.8 metres depth, while work in the shallower 700 zone outlined a potential 200-by-100-metre expansion area beyond the resource model, Wesdome said in a release Monday . The results will feed into a reserve and resource update in the first half of 2027.
“Results are incrementally positive and outline high-grade gold in less explored and shallower parts of the mine, supporting mine life extension,” RBC Capital Markets mining analyst Harrison Reynolds said late Monday in a note. “Several zones returned high grades over meaningful widths near existing infrastructure, which could translate into lower-cost mineable ounces with less incremental development capital.”
The discoveries offer a potential lower-cost route to growth as Wesdome seeks to use spare mill capacity and offset easing grades in its mine plan. The latest results strengthen the case for growth across several zones at Eagle River, about 50 km west of Wawa, National Bank of Canada Capital Markets mining analyst Don DeMarco said in a note Monday evening.
Shares of Wesdome dropped 1.2% to $25.80 Tuesday morning in Toronto, valuing the company at about $3.7 billion (US$2.6 billion). They’ve traded between $19.48 and $37.22 over the past year.
Wider intervals
Other drill results released Monday include hole 26-925-03, which cut 8 metres at 8.3 grams from 262.7 metres depth with no change after capping. The reported intervals are core lengths rather than true widths.
The western extension adds lateral growth potential to earlier evidence that the 800 zone continues at depth, DeMarco said. A previously released surface drill hole intersected mineralization more than 200 metres below the existing zone model, outlining a corridor for further testing in 2027.
“Together these areas could give us more options for where and when we mine. This is growth we can pursue from an operating mine, without the cost or complexity of a greenfield project,” CEO Anthea Bath said.
Elsewhere, drilling between the 800 and 6 Central zones confirmed mineralization first identified in 2025 in drill holes located less than 10 metres from an active ramp. Follow-up work is planned for the first quarter of next year, Wesdome said.
Six growth drill holes in the 700 zone outlined the interpreted expansion area, while other drilling tested the continuity of known mineralization. Four underground exploration drills will continue testing extensions through year-end and into 2027.
Wesdome’s Canadian operations, strong balance sheet and expected free cash flow support spending on exploration and efforts to increase mill utilization, DeMarco said as he maintained his outperform rating and $41 target. Lower grades in the mine plan and the company’s valuation premium remain counterweights to that outlook.
Replacing mined gold
The drilling follows a June update that extended reserve life to eight years at both Eagle River and the Kiena mine in Quebec. Eagle River held 2.9 million proven and probable tonnes grading 7.3 grams gold per tonne for 676,000 oz. as of Dec. 31, 2025.
Wesdome is pursuing a similar strategy at Kiena, where it is testing mineralization close to existing infrastructure while seeking production gains from additional mining areas and operating improvements.
The near-term task is delivering a stronger fourth quarter. Wesdome produced 41,287 oz. in the three months to Sept. 30, missing the 50,500 oz. consensus estimate cited by BMO Capital Markets mining analyst Andrew Mikitchook in an Oct. 13 note.
Eagle River’s throughput rose 10% from the previous quarter, lifting production 13%, Mikitchook said. But blending development and early production ore from Kiena’s Presqu’île zone reduced Kiena’s average grade, weighing on group output.
Wesdome maintained annual guidance of 180,000–205,000 oz., while expecting to finish below the midpoint. That implies roughly 50,000–62,000 oz. in the fourth quarter, compared with its previous quarterly record of about 50,500 oz., Canaccord Genuity said in an Oct. 14 summary of mining analyst Jeremy Hoy’s research.
The company will report third-quarter financial results after markets close on Wednesday.

Infrastructure provider Africa Finance Corp. (AFC) has joined with the Green Climate Fund (GCF) to launch the Africa Sovereign Climate Facility (ASCF), a $690-million effort to support climate initiatives and speed low-carbon, climate-resilient development across Africa.
The groups signed their pact at a ceremony in South Korea on November 3. The ASCF is designed to help African countries address the growing impacts of climate change while advancing their economic development priorities, with an emphasis on energy projects among others. The program will combine technical assistance, capacity building, and large-scale blended finance. Officials said it will integrate climate considerations into national development planning, and accelerate what they call Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs).
Samaila Zubairu, president and CEO of AFC, said, “The infrastructure we build today must both power Africa’s growth and withstand the climate pressures of tomorrow. Through this partnership with GCF, we are combining concessional finance with AFC’s project development expertise and capital to help governments turn national priorities into reliable energy, stronger food and water systems, and resilient infrastructure. Success will be measured in businesses that keep producing, communities better protected and jobs sustained. That is how climate finance becomes an investment in Africa’s lasting prosperity.”
Initial Development Focus
The first phase of the program will focus on project development in Angola, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, and Nigeria. Officials in a news release on Tuesday wrote that those countries “face significant climate vulnerabilities, infrastructure deficits and rising greenhouse gas emissions. Through an integrated, country-led approach, the ASCF will support interventions across critical sectors, including clean energy, health and well-being, food and water security, and climate-resilient infrastructure and the built environment.”
Catherine Koffman, GCF Regional Director for Africa, said, “The Africa Sovereign Climate Facility will help Angola, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire and Nigeria turn national climate priorities into investable projects in clean energy, resilient infrastructure, food systems and water security. GCF’s $280 million [USD] is designed to work alongside substantial co-financing, reaching an estimated 4.5 million people and avoiding 3.4 million tonnes of emissions. This partnership shows how blended finance can strengthen sovereign investment systems and deliver climate capital at scale.”
The launch builds on AFC’s longstanding partnership with GCF to mobilize climate finance and advance sustainable infrastructure development across Africa. In 2023, GCF committed $253 million to AFC Capital Partners’ Infrastructure Climate Resilient Fund (ICRF), supporting the development of climate-resilient infrastructure as an investable asset class, and helping catalyze additional investment from institutional and private-sector investors. The groups said their collaboration “reflects a shared commitment to using innovative financing structures to address Africa’s infrastructure needs while strengthening resilience to climate change.”
Parallel Commercial Facility
AFC as part of its participation in the ASCF will arrange and fully fund a parallel commercial facility of up to $260 million, for a 10-year period, for Angola, Benin, Côte d’Ivoire, and Nigeria through the countries’ respective finance ministries. Officials said the facility “will complement concessional climate financing, expanding the capital available to support eligible investments while helping participating governments integrate climate resilience and low-carbon development into national planning.”
Officials noted that over its lifetime the ASCF “is expected to reduce, avoid, remove or sequester approximately 5.78 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO 2 e) in greenhouse gas emissions— roughly equivalent to removing 1.3 million cars from the road for one year. The programme is also expected to reach 5.2 million beneficiaries through climate adaptation interventions, equivalent to the current estimated population of Cape Town, South Africa.”
Climate analysts have said that Africa is particularly exposed to the effects of climate change, “with rising temperatures, increasingly unpredictable rainfall and more frequent extreme weather events threatening livelihoods, food and water security, infrastructure and economic productivity.” The continent’s rapid population growth, and increasing urbanization of its population, continue to pressure public services and infrastructure, which officials have said reinforces the urgency of embedding climate resilience into the continent’s development.
The groups involved in Tuesday’s launch said the program reinforces AFC’s commitment to mobilizing capital and deploying innovative financing solutions to address Africa’s infrastructure needs, while in turn supporting sustainable, inclusive, and climate-resilient economic growth. AFC officials said that the group’s partnership with the Green Climate Fund will help it bridge the gap between Africa’s climate ambitions and the financing required turn those plans “into tangible development outcomes.”
— Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

There's a New Single-Cylinder Norton Motorcycle in Town, 450 urban Literally Belongs on City Streets
18 photos
Photo: Norton
It's been six years or so since British bike maker Norton was brought back from the edge of the abyss by TVS Motor Company, and exactly one year since the crew announced its so-called Resurgence strategy. Time well spent, it seems, as the Brits have just announced they are entering a new segment with a brand-new bike.
At the Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan, Italy, a new contender in the A2 category was unveiled. It's called the 450 urban (spelled exactly like that, with a lowercase "u"), and it targets the kind of riders who would usually not go for the likes of the Manx and Atlas.
Described as the father of a whole new generation of accessible urban exploration and commuting machines, the single-cylinder motorcycle has become the company's entry-level bike, but promises the same thrills as its bigger siblings.
Norton used an aluminum frame as a skeleton for the two-wheeler, and dressed it in a design that's at least in part inspired by the 1927 Norton CS1, a TT replica road bike that in some circles has a sort of cult following.
Neither naked nor fully faired, the urban kind of looks like many of the electric motorcycles that have popped up in recent years. One of the versions (there will be two of them) moves on 17-inch cast wheels painted in silver, the same color chosen for the frame, and are shod in road tires. The other uses black cast wheels and a grey frame.
Power for the rides comes from a liquid-cooled single-cylinder engine. True to the name the bike wears, it displaces 454cc, and it's only good for 46 horsepower at 8,000 rpm and 45 Nm of torque at 6,000 rpm, making it ideal for A2 license holders.
To aid people in the operation of the motorcycle, the engine is tied to a six-speed transmission with a quickshifter and draws its fuel from a three-gallon (12-liter) tank designed in a very angular fashion.
The suspension system the bike relies on is not some fancy setup capable of taking on rough trails, because that's not what the urban is all about. Instead, we're dealing with a fully adjustable 43 mm KYB upside-down fork at the front and a KYB rear monoshock that's adjustable for rebound and pre-load at the rear. ByBre hardware provides the stopping power.
Targeting a curb weight of 397 pounds (180 kg), the urban does not cut corners when it comes to extra fittings, so it'll ship to customers at an undisclosed point in the future with extended protective gear better suited for off-road motorcycles: mudguards, handguards, and fork protectors, among others.
Norton does not say how much it will charge for the 450 urban, or when we should expect it to get here. We'll keep an eye on things, though, and report back once we know more.

As oil analyst Rory Johnston said in his X feed, “The challenge remains that while any one diplomatic headline hope is very unlikely to amount to much, the market’s base case remains that this will end via some kind of deal.”
Even if the latest news does not mark a significant movement toward some sort of rapprochement, Johnson said “you gotta kind act accordingly so you don’t get run over as this latest episode runs its course.”

Nussir project in Norway. ( Image courtesy of Blue Moon Metals. )
By: Staff Writer November 3, 2026
ACG Metals (LSE: ACG) has agreed to buy Blue Moon Metals’ (TSXV: MOON; Nasdaq: BMM) Norwegian business for $220 million (C$307 million) in shares, adding an Arctic copper project while its existing operation in western Türkiye faces a delayed ramp-up.
The acquisition includes about 95% of Nussir, an underground copper project under construction near Hammerfest in northern Norway. Blue Moon would receive about 8.85 million ACG shares, representing 28% of the enlarged company before dilution, under the agreement announced Tuesday.
“The combination of the Gediktepe operations in Türkiye and Blue Moon’s Norwegian assets is a transformational transaction that creates a fast-growing European copper champion with industry-leading free cash flow margins,” ACG chairman and CEO Artem Volynets said in a statement.
The purchase advances Volynets’ plan to build a copper producer through acquisitions, outlined in a 2024 TNM interview . But it adds another construction commitment just days after ACG disclosed that expanded tailings and water-management work had delayed commercial sulphide production at Gediktepe until early next year.
ACG shares traded 16% stronger at £16.50 late Tuesday in London, valuing the company at about £382 million ($513 million). Blue Moon traded 3.3% weaker at C$5.21 mid-Tuesday in Toronto, giving it a market value of about C$565 million.
Shareholder payout
Blue Moon intends to focus on its U.S. critical-minerals assets while retaining exposure to Norway through ACG. The consideration shares, priced at £18.70 each using ACG’s 30-day volume-weighted average, are expected to be distributed to Blue Moon shareholders within 12 months of closing.
No concurrent financing is required to complete the acquisition, although funding Nussir’s remaining construction costs is a separate requirement. Blue Moon will repay amounts drawn under its Nussir financing package at closing, the company said in its sale announcement .
ACG estimates $126 million remains to be funded at Nussir and is assessing financing proposals, potentially including refinancing its Nordic bonds.
The buyer reported financial net debt of $185 million at Sept. 30, comprising a $200-million Nordic bond less $15 million in cash and doré held at a refinery.
Turkish setback
Gediktepe, about 250 km south of Istanbul in Balıkesir province, was ACG’s first acquisition in its copper consolidation strategy. The mine has produced gold and silver while the company develops sulphide processing to recover copper and zinc.
Heavy rainfall and greater-than-expected volumes of unconsolidated material increased excavation requirements for tailings works fivefold, to about 6 million cubic metres, ACG said in its Oct. 29 update .
The processing plant has completed cold and hot commissioning, but the additional works have delayed the ramp-up. Tailings work is targeted for completion by year-end, weather permitting, with full commercial production expected in the first quarter of 2027.
ACG’s revised 2026 guidance covers only its oxide operation, which is processing existing stockpiles. Updated sulphide guidance is due next year.
Arctic development
Nussir targets first copper concentrate in the first half of 2028. ACG forecasts combined output exceeding 50,000 tonnes of copper equivalent annually over 2029–2033, including all of Nussir. The buyer aims to acquire the remaining minority interest within a year of closing.
The Norwegian portfolio also includes Ulveryggen and exposure to Sulitjelma. A proposed combination of Sulitjelma interests would leave Blue Moon Norway with about 30% of an enlarged business if completed before the acquisition; otherwise ACG would retain NSG, subject to the agreements.
Nussir’s permits remain valid, according to the companies, but its planned marine-tailings disposal has faced scrutiny.
In an August response , Blue Moon rejected short-seller Viceroy Research’s claim that a Norwegian court judgment concerning the separate Engebø project would lead to revocation of Nussir’s permit. Blue Moon said the judgment did not invalidate Nussir’s approvals.
Norway’s government would consider whether the judgment had implications for Nussir, Blue Moon acknowledged at the time. The company said it had received no notification of a comparable challenge against its subsidiary.
Closing conditions
Shareholders representing about 81% of ACG have committed to support the required resolutions, above the 75% threshold. Blue Moon shareholder approval is not required. Closing is targeted for Nov. 30, subject to exchange, regulatory and other conditions.
ACG forecasts combined annual asset-level earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $370 million and free cash flow of $267 million over 2029–2033. Those projections include all of Nussir, exclude corporate costs and financing, and do not represent cash available for shareholder distributions.

BMW Launching Major Driver Assistance Upgrade for 3 Series, 7 Series, iX3, iX4, and X5 Range in 2027
19 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW has confirmed a pretty substantial driver assistance upgrade for select models based on the Cluster Architecture and the Neue Klasse platform. Starting in Germany from 2027 with the iX3, iX3, X5, 3 Series, and 7 Series , the latest iteration of the system supports navigation-guided urban assistance.
All of the aforementioned models, including the Neue Klasse-based i3 sedan and upcoming wagon, already have the necessary hardware for urban driver assistance functions. While highway setups have become increasingly capable in the past few years, few automakers offer Level 2 systems that are capable of handling the urban jungle's more dynamic and challenging driving scenarios.
The Level 2 system of these Bimmers can assist with urban lane changes, turning maneuvers, navigating roundabouts, and right-of-way situations. Active route guidance through BMW Maps also needs mentioning, with BMW Maps allowing the subject vehicle to anticipate the next maneuver instead of reacting to lane markings and traffic around it.
Having mentioned that, we must remind ourselves that BMW already offers automated stopping and starting at traffic lights through its City Assistant in certain markets. The new urban-centric functions that will be introduced next year expand that capability, and the company's endgame is pretty clear. More specifically, BMW intends to combine Motorway Assistant with City Assistant into a continuous nav-guided experience.
Nobody should confuse that with the act of handing the keys to the car and checking emails while said car does all the driving itself. The Munich-based manufacturer clearly states the system is a Level 2 affair, meaning that drivers must intervene whenever necessary. That also means the driver must remain attentive to what's happening in front and around the vehicle rather than checking emails or sleeping behind the wheel.
Photo: BMW To ensure the driver remains engaged with the act of driving, BMW Symbiotic Drive enables the assistance system and driver to work together instead of competing for control. Think of it this way: when assistance operates, the driver can still brake, accelerate, and steer according to their respective preferences. The system is programmed to interpret their steering behavior and the direction of their gaze to understand the driver's intentions.
This, in turn, makes us consider a lane-keeping assist scenario. A driver who deliberately moves toward a lane marking should not receive the same intervention from the system as someone who has inadvertently drifted out of their lane. Put otherwise, BMW's next iteration of the Level 2 system includes software that distinguishes between intentional driver inputs and situations that genuinely require assistance.
BMW's Panoramic iDrive setup also plays a role in the grand scheme of things, for Panoramic Vision displays all specific assistance information directly in the driver's field of vision. The central infotainment system, meanwhile, gains a three-dimensional BMW Maps with Driver Assistance view that combines navigation guidance, the vehicle's surroundings, and information about which Level 2 functions currently operate.
Although we do know said functions will drop by over-the-air updates, BMW hasn't disclosed whether customers have to pay separately for every additional capability or whether some functions will be locked within existing assistance packages. Oh, and by the way, regulatory approval currently stands between the Bavarian automaker and the rollout to customer vehicles.
Technical requirements are said to have been met, subject to official confirmation in early 2027. The BMW system has a few competitors out there, starting with Tesla's Assisted Driving (a.k.a. Full Self-Driving outside Europe) and Stuttgart's MB.Drive Assist Pro. Over at Audi, the Volkswagen Group's closest equivalent is called Adaptive Driving Assistant Plus.
