This 2021 BMW 540i M Sport Just Sold for $26,750 and It's Probably a Best-Buy
19 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
I think I'm being as objective as possible when I tell you that you're looking at peak executive sedan here. Not just regarding something with a BMW badge, but in general. You won't find this combination of driving dynamics and interior build quality in anything else from this segment. Not in the newer G60 5 Series, and certainly not in anything with an Audi or Mercedes badge.
I'll admit that the latest E-Class, the W214, is best-in-class when it comes to comfort, but that's always been the case with Mercedes. You know what you're getting, and it depends on which factors matter most to you. But from a driver's perspective, the G30 5 Series is about as good as it gets.
Regarding this car here, the spec is almost identical to my own - except I have a 530i not a 540i, but the model year is the same and so are tons of other things available on this car, such as the M Sport brakes, the M Sport package, M Sport suspension, the seats, and so on. When new, this car retailed for roughly $70,000, and someone just bought it at auction for $26,750 with 86,340 miles (139,000 km) on the clock.
According to the ad, the coolant, brake fluid and engine oil were all serviced back in August of this year, which means this is about as safe a buy as you can find - mileage be damned. These are extremely reliable drivetrains (the B58 / 8-speed auto combo) and the fact that this car is rear-wheel drive (no xDrive system) makes it all the more safe since you don't have to worry about maintenance for the transfer case.
Aside from its Bernina Gray Amber Effect colorway, this 540i also comes with the Shadowline trim, LED headlights, a power tailgate, sunroof, M Sport bumpers and side skirts (courtesy of the M Sport package), plus a set of Jet Black 19" Style 845M wheels with 245/40 front and 275/35 rear Michelin Pilot Sport 4S tires. So far, it's identical to mine (wheels included), except mine has the Carbon Black Metallic exterior.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Moving along to the interior, highlights include the black perforated SensaTec upholstery, Pearl Chrome accents, heated front seats, wireless charging, a 16-speaker Harman Kardon surround sound system, Gesture Control, wireless charging for your mobile device, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto connectivity, a head-up display, the configurable Live Cockpit Pro gauge cluster, and more.
What's worth keeping in mind about the G30 is that the wireless charging tray isn't particularly large. You can fit a normal iPhone 18 Pro, or something like the iPhone Air. But it's a tight squeeze. The 17 Pro Max and 18 Pro Max? Not a chance. They don't fit.
As for the engine, the B58 is a masterpiece. It's a turbocharged 3.0-liter inline-six unit, rated at 335 horsepower and 332 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via an eight-speed automatic transmission.

Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys New Dodge Challenger Hellcat From Nebraska Dealer for $17,386 Under MSRP
19 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
If you're in the market for a still-new Hellcat-powered Challenger, I think I may have found one of the best deals out there in this TorRed model. Sadly, it's already been sold, but there's nothing stopping you from trying to find another one just like it.
This car was purchased new by the selling dealer at Baxter Chrysler Dodge Jeep Ram in Omaha, Nebraska, for $100,886. That dealer then sold the car at auction for just $83,500 (plus a buyer's fee), but here's the kicker - the odometer read 105 miles. In other words, this thing is still brand spanking new.
As far as I'm concerned, 105 miles is delivery miles. It means the car was moved around a bit from one place to another, probably gassed up, cleaned and so on. This is a new Hellcat for $17,386 below MSRP. It's peak muscle car. I really don't know what more you could want from a Challenger. And don't get me started on the Demon 170 or even the Super Stock. You don't need anything more than a Redeye Jailbreak.
I could argue that you don't need anything more than a base Hellcat , but given where we are today with so many new performance cars hovering around that 1,000 horsepower mark, perhaps 707/717 horsepower might sound a bit "old school", even though it's not. It just goes to show how ridiculous things have gotten on that front. Seems like it was just yesterday that you had to spend millions on a hypercar in order to have over 700 hp.
Anyway, let's take a closer look at the spec on this Challenger, starting with the visuals.
Aside from the TorRed colorway , the car also boasts dual Carbon stripes, a Satin Black SRT Performance spoiler, Brass Monkey badges, HID Air-Catcher headlights, widebody fenders as part of the Widebody package, Redeye badging, a chin spoiler guard, black hood pins, plus a set of 20" Brass Monkey Devil Rim forged wheels with Pirelli P Zero rubber and yellow-finished Brembo calipers. You also get the Widebody competition suspension system with adaptive Bilstein dampers.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Demonic Red Laguna leather seats (heated/ventilated), a rear seat delete, Copper weave carbon fiber trim, a suede headliner, Demonic Red seatbets, an 18-speaker Harman Kardon sound system, and a heated and Alcantara-wrapped steering wheel.
As for performance, here's what's great about this particular spec. Normally, the supercharged high-output 6.2-liter HEMI V8 would have been putting down 797 horsepower and 707 lb-ft of torque. However, thanks to the Jailbreak package , this Challenger is currently hammering out 807 horsepower. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via an eight-speed TorqueFlite automatic gearbox and a limited slip differential.
But what do you guys think? Would you have spent $83,500 (plus a buyer's fee) on this Hellcat? Sound off below.

The Tinytanic Is the World's Smallest Houseboat, Cute and Perfectly Functional
27 photos
Photo: YouTube/David Rule
The real Titanic was the Ship of Dreams, but there's no reason why this tiny boathouse that bares no resemblance to it except for the name inspo shouldn't aspire to be one itself. This is Tinytanic, the world's smallest houseboat and tiniest Ship of Dreams.
Because size isn't always an indicator of might or skill or competence, Tinytanic is, despite its diminutive size, a perfectly functional watercraft that recently completed its maiden journey. It was a short trek but a successful mission: 12 miles (19 km) of floating down Pend Oreille River in Washington, traveling from Metaline Falls to the 233-foot (71-meter) Peeweee Fall.
During this maiden journey, which also doubled as the first buoyancy test as a completed project, Tinytanic proved it was as sound as a boat as it was as a house, which was the idea from the start, since its creator had promised the world's smallest houseboat.
That creator is DIY YouTuber David Rule, famous for his various attempts at creating some of the world's smallest mobile homes , both on land and on water. He doesn't do these projects for the actual records, though, as you probably guessed, but they do help with getting more attention and clicks to the resulting videos.
Photo: YouTube/David Rule David is always up for a dare and a fun project, and Tinytanic proved a little bit of both. The inspiration for it was another houseboat that claimed to be the smallest in the world, Zach Fowlers' rowboat hull that offered about 35 square feet (3.2 square meters) of living space onboard. As with other projects, David tried to make his smaller, while retaining basic functionality.
The Tinytanic came out at 8 feet in length and 3.5 feet in width (2.4 by 1 foot), offering a living footprint of just 28 square feet (2.6 square meters). It's not an official record because David probably did not apply for certification, but it's definitely smaller than the watercraft it was inspired by.
Unlike Fowlers, though, he opted for a pontoon float instead, as he explains in the video at the bottom of the page. Tiny pontoon floats would serve as the base on which he added a cedar platform, on top of which he set out to build the "house part of the houseboat."
Photo: YouTube/David Rule The Tinytanic had to be lightweight in addition to being small, so David used only cedar, pine, and plywood for the construction, with a lick of liquid rubber and a sheet of aluminum for the roofing. Polycarbonate windows, two round ones on each side and an extra-large one on the front of the home for visibility and plenty of natural light , were added after the frame and sidewalls went up.
For a project whose main priority was lightness and compactness, Tinytanic came out surprisingly good-looking inside and out. David combined the two types of wood to add a bit of personality to the build, all the while keeping an eye on structural integrity and durability.
The interior had to be both bedroom and kitchen, with a dedicated storage compartment for the electronics like a 100Ah marine lithium battery and a charge controller. To keep the space from feeling too cramped and to allow ventilation, David opted for a rear wall from zippered tent awning that he could open whenever he wanted to.
Photo: YouTube/David Rule He also added a 12V fan and a small vent to circulate the air inside the tiny cabin . A battery monitor, a USB plug, and an on and off switch for the fan represented the command panel, located by the entry.
Because of the small footprint David worked with, he couldn't make the cabin higher than 42 inches (106 cm), so interior headroom was just enough to sit up. The length of the space was divided into two sections, one of which would hold the bed and the other a three-segment continuous counter that would have to do as a kitchen.
As such, the latter came with a sink with a 12V pump that drew water from the lake and filtered it, before it went into a wastewater "tank" under the sink that was actually an empty juice container. A single-burner butane cooktop, of the removable kind, and a small 12V fridge completed the appliances here.
Photo: YouTube/David Rule David admits that it's no chef's kitchen , but it's just the kind of setup that would work for the basics for the planned three-day trip. Speaking of which, it would be carried out with help from an all-electric 30-lb thrust Minn Kota trolling motor, which David mounted on custom rear wooden brackets.
The two 100W solar panels on the roof powered the motor and everything else inside the cabin, with the exception of the cooktop. David did run into some issues on the second day, when he had to use the motor sparingly because he was running out of battery juice. He also remarked that Tinytanic was exceptionally slow, but also surprisingly stable.
In the end, a build like this one isn't about speed or performance or, for that matter, outstanding comfort . This is still a mobile home in the sense that it has the basic features of a home designed for living in on the road, but it's not meant to be very comfortable or even that good-looking.
Photo: YouTube/David Rule The biggest achievement of a mobile home like Tinytanic is that it exists. So thanks to David for taking us all on this adventure with him.

Here's the V8-Powered 2028 BMW Alpina 7 Series Hitting Over 300 KPH at Nardo
9 photos
Photo: BMW
BMW could have easily made the Alpina-branded 7 Series a performance statement. Instead of creating an M7 under a different name, the German automaker decided that its upcoming flagship sedan model should be able to hit 300 kilometers per hour (186 miles per hour) in superlative comfort.
Pictured under camouflage, the V8-powered newcomer has already exceeded 300 clicks at Nardo. Due to hit dealers in 2027, the BMW Alpina 7 Series is all about comfort, precision, stability, and the ability to cover long distances without exhausting the person behind the wheel or those seated in the back. Put another way, BMW has created a very different sedan from the long-rumored M7.
Equipped with 20-spoke alloys that are unmistakably Alpina in their design, the camouflaged prototype also features production-intent lights and bumpers. The front and rear bumpers, along with the quad oval exhaust finishers, also differentiate this model from its BMW-only equivalent.
BMW says the Alpina-exclusive alloys were developed alongside specific tires, with said tires incorporating a foam layer. That layer is key to high speeds in such a heavy vehicle, with the BMW Alpina 7 Series expected to weigh over two metric tons when equipped with the S68 twin-turbo V8.
What I find even more interesting about said layer is that BMW puts a bigger emphasis on driving comfort and precision rather than outright speed. While anyone can advertise a ridiculously high top speed, few automakers understand that comfort matters a lot more in the long run. Similarly, precision sits really high on the list of priorities of anyone who loves driving.
Photo: BMW BMW hasn't disclosed the maximum output figures of the S68 under its hood, but due to its Alpina branding, look forward to revised accelerator pedal mapping and engine management, all in the name of smoothness and responsiveness over aggressive power and torque delivery. Of course, BMW has recalibrated the ZF-supplied automatic transmission for this application as well.
A comfortable yet dynamic chassis setup also needs highlighting, while aerodynamic tweaks promise stability at Autobahn speeds. Based on the details shared by the Bavarian automaker until now, the BMW Alpina 7 Series isn't chasing one particularly impressive specification. Rather, the automaker wants the engine, tranny, and chassis to work together seamlessly.
Just like the regular 7 Series and a few other BMW models, the BMW Alpina sedan brings navigation-guided driver assistance functions. To be introduced next year, the system can assist with urban lane changes, turns, roundabouts, and in right-of-way situations. BMW further plans to extend its Motorway Assistant concept across country roads and into the urban jungle.
Being a Level 2 system, the driver must remain attentive, ready to take control whenever the situation calls for human intervention. BMW Symbiotic Drive blurs the line between semi-autonomous driving and human intervention, letting the driver accelerate, steer, and brake while the assistance system operates.
Internally referred to as G72, the BMW Alpina 7 Series is expected to enter production in July 2027 for the 2028 model year. Three specifications are understood to launch for 2028, namely the six-pot 740 xDrive, eight-cylinder 760 xDrive, and the zero-emission i7 70 xDrive.
